This is really weird. I am using linux all the time, and it runs fine on
my machine. The point estimates are ok. But vcov seems completely off,
with a negative eigen value of 114.8053. Very strange indeed.

lavaan does not use the Matrix package. But the base matrix functions
rely on BLAS/LAPACK. Are you using the standard 'R' version, or an
external/optimized BLAS/LAPACK stack? You can see this in the output of
sessionInfo()

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Trouble with lavaan on Linux
parts:
On 4/4/25 5:58 PM, 'Peter Haas' via lavaan wrote:
> BLAS:   /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/openblas-pthread/libblas.so.3
> LAPACK: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/openblas-pthread/libopenblasp-
> r0.3.20.so;  LAPACK version 3.10.0

So you are using 'openblas-pthread' instead of the in-house (but
non-optimized) blas/lapack libraries that come with R itself.

The first thing I would try is to compile R again, but with its standard
blas/lapack libraries. As this is the default, and you are starting from
source, this is just a matter of using

./configure
make

Another alternative is to 'switch' the blas/lapack libraries, by making
them point to another set of files. See this blog post:

https://brettklamer.com/diversions/statistical/faster-blas-in-r/

Yves.
